01.title: 1. Requirements
01.text:
# 1. Requirements

SEO Control Center runs on ordinary shared hosting with cPanel. You do **not** need root access, SSH, Docker, Node.js or Redis.

## Hosting

| | Required | Recommended |
|---|---|---|
| PHP | **8.5** (for the website and for cron) | |
| Database | MariaDB 10.6+ or MySQL 8.0+ | |
| PHP extensions | pdo_mysql, curl, mbstring, openssl, **sodium**, zlib, json, filter | intl, zip |
| PHP memory | 128 MB | 256 MB or more |
| PHP execution time | 30 s | 60 s or more |
| HTTPS | yes (AutoSSL / Let's Encrypt is fine) | |
| Cron | every 5 minutes or more often | every minute |
| Disk space | 500 MB free | more if you keep many backups |

Also required:

- your own domain or subdomain, for example `seo.example.com`;
- the option to point its **document root** to a folder of your choice (standard in cPanel).

The installer and *System health* check all of this and tell you exactly what is missing.

## Accounts you may want

- **Google account** with access to your sites in Google Search Console. This is free.
- **DataForSEO account** for search volumes, rank tracking and competitors. You pay DataForSEO per use; see [chapter 6](06-dataforseo.md). The rest of SEO Control Center works without it.
- An **authenticator app** (Google Authenticator, Authy, 1Password …) for two-factor sign-in. Optional, but recommended.

02.title: 2. Installation
02.text:
# 2. Installation

Install SEO Control Center on a **dedicated subdomain**, for example **seo.example.com**. Keep the folder cPanel creates for it. The guided installer handles the application layout automatically; you do not rename an application folder or change the domain path.

## Before you begin

Back up your hosting account. You need PHP 8.5 or newer, MySQL 8+ or MariaDB 10.6+, a valid HTTPS certificate and Cron Jobs access. The launcher also requires cURL, ZIP, sodium, PDO MySQL, mbstring, OpenSSL, filter and zlib, outbound HTTPS, private PHP temporary storage and at least 400 MB free temporary space.

The default-folder flow supports Apache or compatible LiteSpeed hosting with .htaccess and mod_rewrite. The launcher verifies public routing and private-file protection over HTTPS before installing application files. It does not overwrite an existing site. Installation in a website folder such as example.com/seocc is not supported.

## Step 1: Create your subdomain

In **cPanel → Domains → Create a New Domain**:

1. Enter your chosen subdomain, such as **seo.example.com**.
2. Turn off **Share document root** if it appears.
3. Keep the suggested document root and click **Submit**.
4. Note the folder listed next to this subdomain. That is where you upload the installer.

Older cPanel versions may have a separate Subdomains tool. If DNS is managed elsewhere, configure the subdomain at that provider using your hosting server's address. Wait until DNS resolves.

## Step 2: Enable PHP and HTTPS

1. Open **MultiPHP Manager**, select the subdomain, choose **PHP 8.5** or newer and click **Apply**.
2. Your host may use **Select PHP Version** instead. Enable required extensions there; the installer lists anything missing.
3. Open **SSL/TLS Status** or **SSL/TLS Certificates**. Enable AutoSSL or ask your host to install a valid certificate.
4. Open your subdomain over HTTPS. Continue once the browser accepts the certificate.

cPanel may create a PHP-handler .htaccess and a .well-known SSL challenge folder. The launcher preserves recognized PHP handlers and SSL challenge files; it rejects unrelated custom routing rules.

## Step 3: Create an empty database and user

Open **Database Wizard** (older label: MySQL Database Wizard):

1. Create a new database, for example with suffix **seocc**.
2. Create a dedicated database user. Generate a strong password and keep it privately.
3. Select **ALL PRIVILEGES** for that user on this database and finish the wizard.
4. Keep the **full database name**, **full user name** and **password**, including any cPanel prefix such as youruser_.

If you use Manage My Databases instead, also add the user to the database and grant privileges. Use a new database dedicated to SEOcc.

## Step 4: Upload SEOcc

1. Download **scc-<version>-install.zip** from the [latest release](https://github.com/seoccnet/seo-control-center/releases/latest). The file ending in `-install.zip` is the one for new installations.
2. In File Manager, open the document root shown for your new subdomain. The folder must be empty apart from recognized hosting files. Remove a host's placeholder page only after confirming it belongs to this new subdomain.
3. Upload the zip into that folder, select it and choose **Extract**.
4. Open the new **seo-control-center** folder. Turn on **Show hidden files** in File Manager's settings, select everything, and **Move** it up one level into the subdomain's folder.
5. Delete the zip and the empty **seo-control-center** folder.
6. Open **https://seo.example.com/version.json**. It must answer **403 Forbidden**. If you see the file's contents, stop: your host isn't applying `.htaccess`, and private files could be reachable. Ask your host to enable `.htaccess` and `mod_rewrite`.
7. Open **https://seo.example.com**. The installation wizard appears.

There is no document-root change. The `.htaccess` file sends visitors to the `public` folder and blocks the application's private folders.

## Step 5: Follow the workspace wizard

1. **Welcome:** review the hosting checks.
2. **Site & access:** confirm the detected HTTPS subdomain address, and enter the **server setup key**. Copy it from `storage/setup-key.txt` in File Manager. It proves that you control the server's files.
3. **Database:** enter the full database name, database user and password. Usually the host is localhost and the port is 3306.
4. **Your account:** enter your name, email, a password of at least 12 characters and your company or agency name for the first workspace.
5. **Review & install:** review your details and choose the cron interval your host allows. Every five minutes is recommended. Click **Install SEO Control Center** and keep the page open.

The database is checked before setup writes configuration or creates tables. If validation fails, non-password fields are kept; enter passwords again before retrying. Without JavaScript, all sections remain available in one form.

## Step 6: Add cron and finish

1. Keep the completion page open. It shows the schedule and command generated for your actual installation path.
2. Open **cPanel → Cron Jobs**. Choose the same interval you selected in SEOcc. Every five minutes is **Minute: */5**, with **Hour, Day, Month and Weekday: ***.
3. Copy the **command from the completion page** into Command and click **Add New Cron Job**. If your host uses a different PHP executable, ask for its PHP 8.5 command-line path. Do not add duplicate jobs.
4. The wizard saves CRON_INTERVAL_MINUTES automatically. No .env edit is needed for this new-install flow.
5. Download the encryption key from the exact path shown on the completion page and keep an offline copy. Database backups do not contain it.
6. Keep the application's .htaccess files.
7. Sign in.
8. After the first scheduled run, check **System → Health → Cron**. For five-minute cron, allow about 5–10 minutes.

## Recommended: Configure email

Under **System → E-mail**, enter your SMTP settings and send a test message. Your host's Email Accounts → Connect Devices screen provides the outgoing mail settings. This enables invitations and password resets.

Then connect your integrations and add your first project.

## Existing installations

Existing SEOcc workspaces use **System → Updates**, following the [backup and update guide](10-backups-and-updates.md).

04.title: 4. First steps
04.text:
# 4. First steps

## Start with the Quest Log: Chapter 1, Foundations

Open **Quest Log** in the navigation after signing in. Its first chapter, **Foundations**, walks you through setup in seven steps:

1. **Keep background tasks running:** the once-per-minute cron job (installation administrator).
2. **Add your website.**
3. **Connect Google Search Console** (optional).
4. **Connect DataForSEO and set a budget** (workspace owner or administrator).
5. **Choose your keywords.**
6. **Switch on rank tracking.**
7. **See your first results.**

Foundations reads your current settings live, so you can leave and return without losing progress, and a step can go back to **Needs attention** later, for example when Google is disconnected, cron stops or a budget is used up. Each step shows one of these statuses: **Ready**, **Needs setup**, **Needs attention**, **Waiting for first results** or **Optional**. Open **Tips and details** on a step for why it matters, what you will learn, pro tips, common mistakes and a link to the matching guide chapter.

Choose the website you want to set up at the top of the chapter. **Setup guide** in any project header opens Foundations for that website. The dashboard and the project overview show a small Quest Log card with your next step; **Hide this card** hides it for you in this workspace, and you can show it again from the Quest Log. Old **Get started** links and bookmarks open Foundations.

Steps your role can't perform, such as cron, the Google app or the DataForSEO connection for a member, are marked **Handled by your administrator**. They still show their live status, so you can see why imports aren't running, but they don't count against your own progress.

Google Search Console is optional if you want to start directly with keyword rankings. DataForSEO uses your own paid account: set a monthly spending limit before adding keywords, since keyword metrics can already trigger paid background work. Tracking starts only when you enable it on the Rankings page; the Quest Log never switches it on for you and never starts paid work.

“Waiting for first results” means setup has started but no results have arrived yet. Imports and ranking checks run through your hosting's cron job. “Needs attention” points you toward the connection, results page or system health check that needs help.

The progress card highlights your next required step. A zero or exhausted spending limit, a last account check reporting no credit, or sandbox mode needs attention before real paid tracking can run. Sandbox results are sample data. If your license doesn't include Search Console imports or rank tracking, those steps are simply left out; while the license is inactive they stay visible and explain that the work is paused until it is activated. Stored results stay available, and the results shortcut opens the source that actually has data. After changing Search Console properties, Foundations waits for data from the newly linked property.

When every step you can perform is ready, you earn the **Navigator** rank and can continue with the next chapters. See [the Quest Log](26-quest-log.md) for the whole campaign.

## Create a project

A **project** is one website.

1. Go to **Projects → New project**.
2. Enter a name and the domain (for example `example.com`).
3. Choose the time zone your reports should use.

The project opens on its **Overview**. With no saved results, **No imported results yet** links to the sources that fill the dashboard. Start with:

1. **Link Google Search Console:** clicks, impressions and positions ([chapter 5](05-google-search-console.md)).
2. **Add keywords:** the search terms you care about.
3. **Switch on rank tracking:** your Google positions for those keywords ([chapter 6](06-dataforseo.md)).
4. **Add competitors:** compare visibility and find gaps ([chapter 7](07-competitors-and-opportunities.md)).

## The project pages

| Tab | What you see |
|---|---|
| **Overview** | Search movement, recorded organic outcomes, evidence-backed priorities and risks, with observation dates and source coverage |
| **Performance** | Search Console clicks, impressions, CTR and position; charts; top queries, pages, devices and countries (7 days to 16 months) |
| **Keywords** | Your keywords with search volume, CPC and competition; suggestions from Search Console queries you are not tracking yet |
| **Rankings** | Visibility, average position, top 3/top 10, winners and losers, and the full keyword table with history per keyword |
| **Competitors** | Their visibility on your keywords, where they are ahead, and your gaps |
| **Opportunities** | Prioritised to-dos with the data behind each one |
| **Settings** | Name, domain, time zone, Search Console link, deleting the project |

## Exporting to CSV

**Keywords**, **Rankings**, **Opportunities** and the query and page tables on **Performance** have an **Export CSV** button. The file contains what you are looking at:

- **Rankings:** the selected position filter (for example only the top 3), with the latest position of every keyword, not just the current page.
- **Opportunities:** the selected status and type.
- **Performance:** the selected date range, up to 5,000 queries or pages.

The files open directly in Excel, Google Sheets and Numbers: UTF-8, comma separated. Anyone who can see a project can export its data.

## Reports

The **Reports** tab shows a project's report for a week (Monday to Sunday) or a calendar month, compared with the period before. It covers:

- Google + Bing clicks, impressions and CTR, and the average position;
- clicks per day;
- the top 10 pages and queries;
- rankings: visibility, top 3 and top 10, winners and losers;
- the open opportunities.

**Download PDF** saves the report as a PDF file with your report sections and branding. **Print** uses your browser's print dialog. **← Earlier** and **Later →** move between periods.

**By e-mail:** set a schedule, weekly or monthly, with up to 10 recipients; recipients need no account. Each report e-mail includes the PDF as an attachment.

- **Timing:** weekly reports go out on Wednesday at 07:00 and monthly reports on the 3rd at 07:00, in the project's time zone, once Search Console and Bing have the last days.
- **Format:** the e-mail shows the key figures as a formatted report, with a plain-text version for mail programs that prefer it, and links to the full report. The link needs a sign-in.
- **Testing:** *Send a test report to me* shows what recipients get.

E-mail must be set up under *System → E-mail*.

**Customize client reports:** in Reports, project editors choose the included search, rankings, GA4, audit and opportunity sections. The selection applies to printable reports and both email formats. Workspace managers can set a report brand name, accent and footer shared by all projects in that workspace. Blank fields inherit installation branding. Upload a PNG/JPEG/WebP logo (up to 512 KB, 16–2,000 pixels per side) for printable reports; emails use text branding without loading images. Separate client workspaces can therefore have separate report brands.

## Alerts and the weekly digest

SEO Control Center watches your projects and e-mails you when something needs attention. It checks every hour and sends each alert once:

- **Ranking drop:** keywords that fell out of the top 10 since the previous rank check;
- **Traffic drop:** clicks down 30% or more in the last 7 days compared with the 7 days before (from at least 100 clicks);
- **Site audit errors:** a new audit found more errors than the one before;
- **Lost backlinks:** strong referring domains (domain rank 30+) in the latest lost-links lookup;
- **DataForSEO budget:** the month will exceed the budget, or the balance lasts less than a week. Only owners and admins get this one.

The **weekly digest** arrives on Monday morning, one e-mail per workspace. For each project you can see, it shows clicks, top 10 keywords, site health, winners and losers, the top open opportunities, the week's alerts and a link to the weekly report.

Under **Your account → Notifications** you can turn alerts and the digest on or off, choose which alerts you get and mute projects. You can also add a short **AI summary** at the top of the digest. It is written by the workspace's AI assistant and counts against its budget. The page also lists the alerts of the last 30 days.

Alerts only use data that is already in SEO Control Center. They don't trigger paid lookups.

Project editors can tune alert thresholds in Notifications. Integration managers can optionally send future project alerts to Slack or a generic HTTPS JSON endpoint; see [Alerts and weekly digest](17-alerts-and-digest.md) for setup, security and delivery limits.

## Adding keywords

1. Go to **Keywords**.
2. Paste one keyword per line, up to 1,000 per project.
3. Choose the country and language, then click **Add keywords**.

Search volume, CPC and competition are fetched from DataForSEO in the background, if it is connected. Metrics are reused for 30 days, so they are not paid for twice.

**Tip:** the **Suggestions from Search Console** box lists queries that already bring you impressions. Tick them and add them with one click.

## Background work

Imports, rank checks and analyses run in the background with cron, usually within a few minutes. The page shows what is queued or running. If something seems stuck, look at **System → Jobs** ([chapter 11](11-troubleshooting.md)).

05.title: 5. Connecting Google Search Console
05.text:
# 5. Connecting Google Search Console

SEO Control Center reads your Search Console data with **read-only** access and stores it on your server. The charts load from your own database, not from Google.

Connecting has two parts:

1. **Once per installation:** create a Google "app" (OAuth client). This takes about 10 minutes, and only the administrator does it.
2. **Per workspace:** connect a Google account, then link each project to its property.

Open **Integrations → Connection guides** for an illustrated Search Console walkthrough with original Google screenshots, verification links and direct setup links. The administrator’s **System → Google app** page has a separate OAuth guide. Other provider guides are available on their settings pages.

## Part 1: The Google app (administrator, once)

In the [Google Cloud Console](https://console.cloud.google.com/):

1. **Create a project**, for example "SEO Control Center".
2. **APIs & Services → Library:** search for **Google Search Console API** and click **Enable**.
3. **APIs & Services → OAuth consent screen** (also called *Google Auth Platform*):
   1. Choose the audience appropriate for your users (External for accounts outside your Google Workspace organization). Enter the app name, your support e-mail and your domain.
   2. Scopes: add `.../auth/webmasters.readonly`.
   3. In **Testing**, add the intended Google accounts as test users. Refresh tokens for this access can expire after seven days. Follow Google's publishing and verification requirements for your app's audience before moving to production.
4. **APIs & Services → Credentials → Create credentials → OAuth client ID:**
   - Application type: **Web application**.
   - **Authorized redirect URI:** `https://seo.example.com/integrations/google/callback`. Use your own domain, exactly as in the site address.
5. Copy the **Client ID** and **Client secret**.

In SEO Control Center, go to **System → Google app**, paste both values and save. The secret is stored encrypted.

If Google blocks consent, review the app audience, test-user list, authorized redirect URI and any required verification in Google Auth Platform. Confirm that the OAuth client belongs to this SEOcc installation before approving access.

## Part 2: Connect your Google account

1. Go to **Integrations → Connect a Google account**.
2. Sign in with the Google account that has access to your sites in Search Console, and allow access.
3. Your properties appear in the list. **Refresh properties** reloads them after you add a site in Search Console.

## Part 3: Link a project

1. Open the project and go to **Settings → Google Search Console → Manage link**.
2. Choose the property: a domain property (`sc-domain:example.com`) or a URL property.

The first import starts right away:

- The most recent days arrive within minutes.
- Up to **16 months** of history follow over the next hours.
- After that, new data is imported every 6 hours. Google's data is 2–3 days behind, as in Search Console itself.

With each import SEOcc also reads:

- **Latest days, not final yet:** Google's early numbers for the last two or three days, shown in their own table on **Performance**. Today's row is marked *today so far*. These numbers change a little until Google finalizes them; then they move into the normal figures. The Overview prognosis shows them next to its projection; comparisons, forecast training and opportunities use final data only.
- **Other Google surfaces:** clicks and impressions from **Discover**, **Google News**, the **News tab**, **image search** and **video search**, compared with the previous period. They are not included in the web search figures. A surface only appears when it had impressions.
- **Sitemaps:** each sitemap Google knows for the property, with errors, warnings and when Google last read it. See **Google indexing** in the project.

## Bing Webmaster Tools

Bing's index also powers Yahoo, DuckDuckGo and Ecosia, and the web search of ChatGPT and Copilot. Connecting it is free and takes a few minutes.

1. Sign in to [Bing Webmaster Tools](https://www.bing.com/webmasters) and add your site. **Import from Google Search Console** there does it in one step, verification included.
2. In Bing Webmaster Tools, open **Settings** (top right) → **API Access** → **API Key**, accept the terms and click **Generate API Key**.
3. In SEO Control Center, go to **Integrations → Bing Webmaster Tools**, paste the key and click **Connect Bing**. The key is checked with Bing and stored encrypted.
4. In the project, go to **Settings → Bing Webmaster Tools → Manage link** and choose the site.

The first import runs within minutes, then twice a day. Open **Performance** and switch to **Bing** to see clicks and impressions per day and the top queries and pages.

Bing also appears on the project **Overview**, as a row under the Google figures. The dashboard's project cards add Bing's clicks and impressions to Google's and show the split, for example *Google 323 · Bing 13*.

**How Bing's data differs from Google's:**

- **History:** about six months.
- **Daily totals:** clicks and impressions only. Bing reports positions for queries and pages, not for the whole site per day.
- **Queries and pages:** reported per week. The tables cover the full weeks that end in the selected range.
- **Crawl & index:** below the queries and pages, the Bing view shows how many of your pages are in Bing's index and how that changed in the period, how many pages Bing crawled, crawl errors and pages blocked by robots.txt. **Most linked pages** lists the pages other sites link to, as Bing counts them. It's free, but Bing-only; **Backlinks** has the fuller picture.
- **No recent data:** Bing only reports days with impressions. If the newest data is more than two weeks old, the Bing view says so; check the site's indexing in Bing Webmaster Tools (Site Explorer, URL Inspection).

## IndexNow

IndexNow tells Bing and the other participating engines (Yandex, Seznam, Naver and more) right away when a page is new or has changed. Google does not take part.

1. In the project, go to **Settings → IndexNow → Manage** and click **Set up IndexNow**.
2. Click **Download key file** and upload the file to the root folder of your website (with cPanel: File Manager → `public_html`), so it opens at `https://your-domain/<key>.txt`.
3. Click **Check key file**.
4. Enter your sitemap address and tick **Submit new and changed URLs automatically**. Every 6 hours the sitemap is read. The first check only records the URLs; after that, new pages and pages with a changed `lastmod` are submitted.
5. **Submit URLs now** sends up to 1,000 addresses by hand, for example after a larger update.

Leave the key file on your site. The results of every submission are listed on the page.

### WordPress companion

Project Overview shows integration managers an optional **Use WordPress? Meet SEOcc** notice with a download and setup link. **Hide this notice** remembers dismissal for your user and project in this browser. The permanent explanation, installation steps and download remain in **Settings → IndexNow**, even after dismissal. Viewing or hiding the notice installs nothing and sends no notification.

For a WordPress website, choose **Download SEOcc WordPress plugin** on SEOcc's IndexNow page. Upload the ZIP in WordPress **Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin**, activate it and open **Settings → SEOcc**. Paste the key generated by this SEOcc project and save. Open the displayed key-file URL, then use **Check key file** in SEOcc. After verification, explicitly enable notifications in WordPress.

The plugin serves the key URL without writing a website file. It requires a public HTTPS Home address, WordPress 6.5+ and PHP 8.1+. In a multisite network, SEOcc can be network-activated, but each site has its own Settings → SEOcc: paste the key of the SEOcc project for that site's domain on every site you want to notify. Archived, spam and deleted sites send nothing. With a subdirectory Home address such as `https://example.com/blog/`, the key URL is `https://example.com/blog/{key}.txt` and only URLs under `/blog/` are notified; enter `/blog/` as the **Site path** when you choose **Check key file** in SEOcc. SEOcc's own manual and sitemap submissions then also send only URLs under that path. If the host intercepts `.txt` requests, use the manual key-file method or correct routing first.

WordPress queues notifications for public content changes, permalink changes and removal of previously public content through WP-Cron, with at most three retries for temporary failures. Draft/private/password-protected content, revisions, autosaves and attachments are excluded. Activation does not submit existing content. The last notification result appears in WordPress; these direct submissions are separate from SEOcc's submission history and sitemap jobs. Enabling both may duplicate notifications. Disabling notifications or deactivating the plugin cancels pending plugin work.

## Good to know

- **Totals versus rows:** the query and page tables leave out anonymised queries, as Search Console does, so they add up to less than the totals.
- **Disconnecting** revokes access at Google and keeps all imported data.
- **"Needs reconnection":** Google withdrew access (password change, revoked access, or an app still in *Testing*). Click **Connect** again. Imports resume by themselves.

06.title: 6. DataForSEO: keywords, rankings, research, local SEO and backlinks
06.text:
# 6. DataForSEO: keywords, rankings, research, local SEO and backlinks

Search volumes, rank tracking, keyword research, AI mentions, local SEO and backlinks come from **DataForSEO**, a data provider you pay per use. You use your own DataForSEO account: SEO Control Center adds no markup, and you only pay for what you use.

## Interrupted lookups

Domain overviews, backlink profiles, AI mention metrics and AI answer samples save each completed request, including responses with no matches. A safe temporary failure retries only the unfinished requests. Previous published results remain visible until the entire lookup completes.

If the budget is reached or queue retries run out, use the same lookup button with the same settings after resolving the problem. Completed requests are reused. Changing the domain, competitors or locale starts a fresh lookup; a completed lookup also starts fresh when requested again. Failed weekly/monthly batches can be resumed manually with the same analysis settings.

A timeout, interrupted worker, malformed paid result or uncertain charge stops resumption. Review DataForSEO usage before another paid lookup; SEOcc blocks an identical request while its outcome is unresolved. This prevents a silent second purchase. Progress cannot be recovered for failures that occurred before this feature saved checkpoints.

## Connect

1. Create an account at [dataforseo.com](https://dataforseo.com/), **verify it**, and top up credit.
2. In the DataForSEO dashboard, open **API Access** and copy the **API login** and **API password**. They are *not* your website password.
3. In SEO Control Center, go to **Integrations → DataForSEO**, paste both values and click **Connect**. The credentials are checked for free and stored encrypted.

If the connection is refused, the page shows DataForSEO's reason, for example an account that is not verified yet. Fix it at DataForSEO, then click **Test connection**.

## Costs

What SEO Control Center uses, at DataForSEO's current list prices. Your DataForSEO dashboard shows the exact prices.

| Action | Roughly |
|---|---|
| Keyword metrics (volume, CPC, competition) | about $0.075 per request of up to 1,000 keywords per country, reused for 30 days |
| Rank check | about $0.015–0.02 per keyword and check (top 100 results) |
| Local check | about $0.002 per local keyword plus $0.005 for the Business Profile |
| Keyword research lookup | $0.012 per lookup plus $0.00012 per returned row (1,000 ranking keywords ≈ $0.13) |

Examples:

- **100 keywords, checked weekly:** about $1.50–2 per week.
- **100 keywords, checked daily:** about $10–14 per week.

Competitor tracking costs **nothing extra**: it uses the results of your rank checks.

## Budgets

**Integrations → DataForSEO → Budget** sets:

- a **daily** limit;
- a **monthly** limit;
- a **maximum per request**.

Before every paid request, SEO Control Center reserves the estimated cost against these limits. A request that would exceed a limit is not sent. The page also shows what was spent today and this month.

## Rank tracking

1. Open the project → **Rankings → Tracking settings**.
2. Switch tracking on and choose the device (desktop or mobile) and how often to check (daily or weekly).

Checks run in the background. **Check now** starts one immediately; keywords already checked today are not checked again.

What the Rankings page shows:

- **Visibility:** your estimated share of possible clicks, weighted by search volume. 100 % means position 1 for every keyword.
- **Winners and losers** compared with the check about a week earlier.
- **History per keyword:** click a keyword to see its position chart, the ranking URL, the SERP features and the Search Console clicks for that exact query.

**Results-page changes** (*Research → Results-page changes*) shows what changed on the results pages of your tracked keywords between two checks on the same device, at most 14 days apart: features such as the AI Overview appearing or disappearing, tracked competitors entering or leaving the top 10 (and whether above you), new URLs of competitors or your own site, you entering, leaving or moving 5 places or more, and the kind of page Google ranks shifting. It counts the last 30 days, lists new URLs and keywords gained and lost per competitor, and can be filtered by change, keyword, domain or URL and dates. Everything comes from your stored checks; nothing extra is bought. A keyword needs two checks before changes appear; a missed check is a gap, not a change.

## Keyword research

**Keywords → Keyword research** looks up data from the DataForSEO keyword database. Each lookup runs in the background and its result is stored, so viewing it again costs nothing. A new lookup replaces the previous result.

| Section | What it shows | Roughly |
|---|---|---|
| Domain overview | organic keywords, top 3/top 10 and estimated monthly traffic of your domain and your competitors | $0.012 per domain |
| Your ranking keywords | up to 1,000 keywords your domain ranks for, including ones you do not track yet | $0.13 |
| Keyword gap | per competitor, up to 500 keywords they rank for and you do not | $0.07 |
| Keyword ideas | up to 300 related keywords for up to 20 seed keywords | $0.05 |
| Competitor discovery | the 20 domains that share the most keywords with you; add them as competitors with one click | $0.01 |

Click a column header to sort a table (click again to reverse the order). Keyword tables also have filters: keyword contains, volume from/to, difficulty up to and position from/to. Sorting and filters cover the whole stored result, not only the rows on the page.

Choose the country and language at the top before starting a lookup. Every country and territory Google Ads targets and every Google Search language is available. When you pick a country, the languages keyword research has data for there are listed first. A lookup in a combination it does not cover (Croatia in English, for example) is refused before anything is paid, and the message names the languages that work. Keyword volumes come from Google Ads, which filters by 48 languages; for any other language, such as Bosnian, the volume is the country's volume across languages. Tick keywords in any table and click **Track selected keywords** to add them to your tracked keywords. Already tracked keywords are marked with ✓.

Lookups need the role *Owner*, *Admin* or *Member*, a connected DataForSEO account and the workspace budget; viewers can read the stored results.

**Research on file** (*Research → Research on file*) lists every paid lookup the project already has: keyword research, gaps, competitors, AI visibility and backlinks, with the market, the seeds or prompts, the date, and whether it is still *current* (30 days). It also lists the topics analyzed with *Why they outrank you* and how many tracked searches have a stored results page. Check it before buying new data.

**Repeated lookups ask first.** If you start a lookup that already ran with the same settings and is still current, SEO Control Center does not buy it again. A notice shows when it ran; choose **Run again and pay** if you really need newer data. A lookup in another market, with other seeds or for another competitor runs as usual.

## Local SEO

**Project → Local** shows where your business appears in Google Maps when people search near a location.

1. **Settings:** enter the business name exactly as on Google Maps, the location your customers search from and the size of the area. To get the location, right-click the spot in Google Maps and click the coordinates at the top of the menu; they are copied, for example `43.8563, 18.4131`.
2. **Local keywords:** add up to 50 searches people make on Google Maps, such as "plumber" or "pizza near me". The place name is not needed, because the search is made at your location.
3. **Check now** (or tick *Check every week*): the check runs in the background and costs about $0.002 per keyword plus $0.005 for your Business Profile.

The page then shows:

- your **position in Google Maps** for each keyword (the top 3 are the places Google shows in the local pack of the normal search results), with the change since the last check;
- the **top 3 businesses** for each keyword with their rating and number of reviews, and the **local competitors** that appear most often;
- your **Business Profile**: category, rating, number of reviews, whether the profile is claimed, address, phone, website, photos and the rating history;
- **Profile and website:** whether your website states the same business name, phone number and address as the profile, whether the profile links to this website, and whether your pages have LocalBusiness structured data. The details come from the latest completed site audit, so run one after you change your site;
- **Review handling:** from the review texts you imported (see *Local branches and reviews*): the share of reviews with an owner reply, critical reviews still waiting for an answer, new reviews per month, and your review count against the local pack;
- **Categories in the local pack:** the primary categories of the other businesses in the top 3, with yours marked. If most of them use a category you do not have, check whether it describes your business.

Differences in these three areas also appear as *Local SEO* findings, each with an action plan.

If your business is not found, check that the name matches Google Maps exactly and that the location is close to it.

### Ranking grid

Google ranks local businesses by distance, so your position changes across a city. **Ranking grid** checks one keyword at a grid of points around your location (3 × 3, 5 × 5 or 7 × 7 points, 250 m to 5 km apart) and shows your position at each point as a coloured map: green for the top 3, amber for places 4–10, orange for 11–20 and red where you are not found. The outlined cell is your location. A grid costs about $0.002 per point; a 5 × 5 grid about $0.05.

## Backlinks

**Project → Backlinks** shows who links to your site and to your competitors, from DataForSEO's link index. Each section has its own button, so you only pay for what you look at:

- **Link profiles:** domain rank (0–100, higher is stronger), referring domains, backlinks, the share of nofollow domains and the spam score for your domain and each competitor. Tick **Check every month** to keep a history; the table then shows the change since the previous check.
- **Referring domains:** up to 500 domains linking to you. Click a column header to sort.
- **New and lost referring domains** of the last 30 days.
- **Link gap:** domains that link to your competitors but not to you, those linking to several competitors first. These are good candidates for outreach. It needs competitors (*Competitors*).
- **Anchor texts:** the link texts other sites use most when they link to you.

Each lookup costs about $0.024 plus a small amount per returned row (a full referring domain list about $0.04) from the workspace budget. The Backlinks API must be activated in your DataForSEO dashboard; if it is not, the lookup shows DataForSEO's error message.

# 7. Competitors and opportunities

## Competitors

Add up to **10 competitors** per project under **Competitors → Add a competitor**, for example `competitor.com`. Their subdomains count as theirs.

**Suggested competitors** lists the domains that appear most often in the top 10 for your keywords. Add them with one click.

For each competitor you see, on your tracked keywords:

- **Visibility** compared with yours;
- **Top 3 / Top 10:** how many of your keywords they rank for there;
- **Ahead of you:** keywords where they rank better;
- **Gaps:** keywords where they are on page one and at least 10 places ahead of you, or you are not in the top 100.

Click a competitor to see the keyword-by-keyword comparison.

Competitor data comes from your rank checks at no extra cost, so history starts when you add a competitor.

## AI visibility

For many searches, Google shows an AI-written answer (an **AI Overview**) above the results and lists the sites it used as sources. **Project → AI visibility** shows, from your rank checks:

- how many of your tracked keywords show an AI Overview;
- in how many of them your site is cited, and at which place among the sources;
- which of your competitors are cited instead;
- the sites cited most often for your keywords.

The figures compare with the check about a week earlier. The data arrives with each rank check; rank tracking must be on. AI Overviews change often and differ by location and device, so watch the trend rather than a single day.

### AI assistants

The **AI assistants** section on the same page shows how ChatGPT and Google's AI answers (AI Overviews and AI Mode) talk about your site, from DataForSEO's database of AI answers:

- **Check mentions** compares how often your domain and each competitor are mentioned or cited, and the AI search volume (the estimated monthly number of questions) behind those mentions. It costs about $0.20 per domain.
- **Find questions** lists the most searched questions whose AI answers mention your domain, with an excerpt of the answer, your place among the sources ("#2") or "mentioned" when you are named but not linked, and the other sites cited. It costs about $0.25.

Both run in the background and are stored, so viewing them again is free. ChatGPT data covers the United States in English; Google's AI answers use your project's market.

Click **Check every week** to run the mention check automatically every 7 days. Each check is kept, and **Your mentions over time** shows how your mentions develop.

**Answers to your prompts** asks Gemini and Perplexity your own questions. Enter up to 10 prompts your customers might ask (one per line, up to 500 characters each) and your brand name, then click **Check answers**. Each prompt goes to both assistants with web search. The table shows, per answer, whether your brand is **Named**, whether your site is **Cited** as a source, which competitors are named or cited, and **Read answer** opens the full answer with its sources. Each prompt is answered once; AI answers change between runs, so treat the result as a sample of today's answers, not as how often you are mentioned. It costs at most $0.06 per answer (usually much less), and what DataForSEO reports is what is charged.

### AI crawler access

AI search tools can only show and cite pages their crawlers may fetch. **AI crawler access** reads your site's `robots.txt` and `llms.txt` (free: only your own site is fetched) and shows, per crawler, whether robots.txt lets it in:

- **Search and answer crawlers** fetch pages so answers can show and cite them: OAI-SearchBot and ChatGPT-User (ChatGPT), PerplexityBot and Perplexity-User, Claude-SearchBot and Claude-User, Googlebot (Google Search, including AI Overviews and AI Mode), Bingbot (Bing and Copilot) and Applebot.
- **Training crawlers** collect text for model training: GPTBot, ClaudeBot, Google-Extended, Applebot-Extended, CCBot and meta-externalagent. Blocking them is your choice and does not stop the search crawlers from citing you.

Each crawler is *Allowed*, *Blocked* (robots.txt disallows the home page) or *Some top pages blocked* (the home page is allowed but one of your 10 most-clicked Search Console pages is not). *Rule used* says whether robots.txt has a group naming the crawler or the crawler falls back to the `User-agent: *` rules. Groups match the crawler's name exactly, so a group for `Applebot` does not apply to `Applebot-Extended`.

The check runs weekly by itself; **Check again** runs it within a few minutes (members who can run analyses). When robots.txt cannot be read (a server error, a rate limit or a timeout), crawlers may stop fetching the site, so nothing is evaluated until it answers again. A firewall or CDN bot rule can still block crawlers that robots.txt allows; this check cannot see that.

`llms.txt` is a short Markdown guide to your most useful pages for AI tools. It is marked *Few published tests*: optional, and no published test has measured an effect on AI answers yet.

A blocked search crawler becomes an **AI visibility** opportunity with a plan to allow it.

### Citation readiness of your top pages

For your 10 most-clicked pages of the last 28 days, **Citation readiness** shows what each offers AI answers to quote, from the latest completed site audit, as *passed / known* checks and a list of what is missing:

| Check | How well tested |
|---|---|
| Names an author | Tested repeatedly |
| Structured data for the content (not only breadcrumbs) | Tested repeatedly |
| Links to sources from the text | Tested repeatedly |
| Facts with figures (percentages, prices, sizes, several numbers in a paragraph) | Tested repeatedly |
| Tables or lists | Tested repeatedly |
| Headings phrased as questions | Some tests, effect varies |
| States when it was updated (`dateModified` or `article:modified_time`) | Some tests, effect varies |
| Opens with a short answer (20 to 80 words) | Few published tests |

The author and source checks count only for articles: pages with Article structured data or `og:type` article, or in a blog, guide, news or similar folder. Product, category and home pages are not expected to name an author or cite sources, so they show the other six checks. Pages crawled before 0.43.0 show only the checks the audit recorded then, with how many checks follow after the next site audit ("Nothing missing so far · 5 checks after the next site audit"). Pages the audit did not crawl are listed as *Not in the latest site audit*.

### Visits from AI assistants

With a linked GA4 property, **Visits from AI assistants** shows the sessions, key events and purchase revenue that ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Copilot, Claude and other assistants sent to your site, in all channels. It compares the last 28 imported days with the 28 days before, per assistant. The data comes with each GA4 import: one extra read-only report, always covering both 28-day windows.

GA4 counts a visit for an assistant only when the assistant passes its address or a `utm_source`. Visits from assistant apps often arrive without one and count as direct traffic, so treat the numbers as a lower bound. A failed AI referral import is shown on the page and never fails the GA4 import.

### Brand-name mentions without a link

The separate **Brand-name mentions** section searches your public name in AI answer text, even without a website citation. Save the name and Google market, then request a paid check or explicitly opt into a separate weekly schedule. Review excerpts for namesakes and compare completed history. Name matches and domain counts overlap; never add them. See [Brand-name mentions](20-brand-name-mentions.md) for setup, costs and failure handling.

## Opportunities

Every 6 hours, SEO Control Center looks for concrete improvements in all the data stored for a project: Search Console and Bing, rank checks, competitors, the site audit, keyword research, backlinks, AI visibility and local SEO.

| Type | Example |
|---|---|
| **Quick win** | A keyword or search query on positions 4–20 with real demand: reaching the top 3 would bring clearly more clicks. Also a search for your own brand where you are not first (see below) |
| **Low click-through rate** | A query or page on page one gets less than half the clicks usual for its position: improve the title and description |
| **Ranking decline** | A tracked keyword that was in the top 20 lost at least 5 positions, or dropped out of the results |
| **Traffic decline** | A page lost at least 30 % of its clicks compared with the period before (from at least 20 clicks) |
| **Competitor gap** | A competitor is on page one and at least 10 places ahead of you for a tracked keyword |
| **Content gap** | Search engines show your site for a search with real demand, but only beyond page two: no page answers it well yet |
| **Technical issue** | The latest site audit found broken pages, missing titles or another error or warning on your site (one entry per issue type, with example pages). Issues on pages that get clicks in Search Console rank higher |
| **Keyword gap** | Competitors rank on page one for a search you do not rank for at all (from *Keywords → Keyword research → Keyword gap*); the more competitors, the more reliable |
| **Link building** | You have far fewer referring domains than your competitors; a strong site links to several competitors but not to you; a strong site stopped linking to you; or many of your links look spammy (from *Backlinks*) |
| **AI visibility** | Google's AI Overview for a tracked keyword cites other sites but not you, although you rank on page one; or ChatGPT or Google's AI mention a competitor far more often than you |
| **Local SEO** | You are not in the local pack (top 3 on Google Maps) for a local keyword; your Business Profile is not claimed, has fewer reviews or a lower rating than the local pack, or is incomplete |
| **Clicks falling, ranking stable** | A search query keeps its position and demand, but clearly fewer people click: the results page changed (for example a new AI Overview). Google data only |
| **Format mismatch** | Most top results for a tracked keyword are a different kind of page than yours, for example category pages while yours is a blog post |
| **Free tool idea** | People search for a calculator, checker, generator or similar tool with real demand, and you are not in the top 3 |
| **Merge near-duplicate pages** | Two pages of the latest site audit have nearly the same text and at least one is shown in search: keep the page with most clicks and redirect the other to it. Listed as *Cannibalization*. Pairs with a product page are never proposed, because different products often share a description. Pairs you mark *Keep separate* in the overlap review are left out too |
| **AI visibility (crawler access)** | robots.txt keeps an AI search or answer crawler (ChatGPT search, Perplexity, Claude, Google, Bing, Apple) out of your home page or of one of your top Search Console pages |
| **AI visibility (prompt gap)** | In your AI answer check, Gemini and Perplexity both recommend the same competitor for a prompt and mention you in neither |
| **Google indexing** | A saved URL Inspection reports an indexing concern for a page that gets impressions; Google indexes another URL than the canonical the page declares; or Google found errors in the page's structured data, so its rich results may not show |
| **Sitemap problems** | Search Console reports errors (or only warnings) for one of your sitemaps |
| **Bing crawl and index** | Bing has at least 10 % and 20 fewer of your pages in its index than four weeks ago, or at least 5 % of the pages Bing crawled returned errors (from at least 20 errors) |
| **Internal links: topic main page** | Pages Google shows for a topic in *Topics & owners* (at least 50 impressions) that do not link from their text to the topic's main page. Only main pages you set under *Page that should own this topic*, or article pages with at least half of the topic's searches, are used |
| **Refresh aging content** | An article (in a blog, news, guide or similar folder) still gets at least 300 impressions at an average position of 20 or better, but your sitemap says it has not been updated for over a year. Needs sitemap last-modified dates from the IndexNow sitemap check |
| **Traffic decline on another Google surface** | Clicks from Discover, Google News, the News tab, image or video search fell by at least 30 % compared with the period before (from at least 20 clicks) |

**Brand searches.** People who search your brand are looking for you, so anything ranking above you there takes clicks that should be yours. SEOcc reports a Google search for your brand, with at least 20 impressions, where your average position is below first.

Your brand words are the project name, unless it is generic, and the main part of your domain. A search counts when one to three of its words, written together, are a brand word, with or without a final "s". For `northwindgoods.test`, "northwind good" and "trail northwind good" both count. These searches are not repeated as ordinary quick wins. The action plan says what to check above you and what to make unmistakable on your home page.

Keyword research also adds **quick wins** for keywords you rank for at positions 4–20 but do not track yet. Where the keyword difficulty is known, it sets the effort of a quick win or keyword gap: up to 30 is low, up to 60 medium, above that high.
With a linked Bing site, Bing's queries and pages are added to Google's before the analysis. A query that is just below a threshold on Google alone can qualify with Bing's demand added. Its evidence then shows the period with *Google + Bing*. Traffic declines compare Google only, because Bing reports pages per week.

Each opportunity shows:

- a **priority**, based on impact, confidence and effort, with a **score breakdown**: demand (the estimated extra clicks), relevance (the BID check and intent), impact, confidence with its reasons, effort, risk (such as zero-click searches) and the data sources it relies on, plus the formula that combines them. Reports show the same figures in one line per opportunity, and AI assistants get the same breakdown over MCP;
- the **data behind it**, such as impressions, current CTR and expected CTR;
- an **estimate** of the extra clicks where possible.

Each action plan says **how well tested** its kind of change is:
- *Tested repeatedly*: several independent published tests measured an effect.
- *Some tests, effect varies*: results differ by site, template or intent.
- *Few published tests*: try it on a few pages with a comparison set first.
- *Search engine guidance*: technical fixes that follow search engine documentation.

Even a well-tested change is not a forecast for your site, so change a group of pages, keep a similar group unchanged, and compare. The label never changes a finding's priority.

**Start a change bundle** on a finding opens a new change bundle (*Manage → Change bundles*) with the finding's page, problem, evidence, expected effect and revert rule filled in, plus empty edit rows for the fields that kind of plan usually changes. Enter the new text, capture the baseline, approve, check the live page and record the deployment. SEOcc then drafts a measurement plan on the recorded change with the matching metric, the page and its query; add control pages there and freeze its baseline.

Each opportunity also has an **Action plan**: what to do about it, filled in with the finding's query and page. It says when the plan applies, what to prepare, what to change (numbered steps), what to keep unchanged so you can see the effect, what to measure and when to revert, plus what to avoid and other ideas to consider. Page action plans show each finding's next step, and team tasks show the full plan. The plan is guidance: it never changes a finding's priority or estimate.

### Business profile and the BID check

Under **Opportunities → Business profile**, describe the business: what kind of business it is, the main goal of search traffic, what it offers (one per line, up to 30), terms that never fit (for example *jobs* or *used*, up to 100), and two limits: the highest keyword difficulty you want to target (default 30) and the strength up to which a competing domain counts as beatable (default 20).

Every keyword finding then shows a **BID check**:

- **Business potential (B, 0–3):** how much a ranking helps your goal. Fixed rules decide, from your goal, the searcher's intent and whether the search mentions what you offer. Job searches and your excluded terms score 0. You can rate any keyword yourself on its finding; your rating wins over the rules. Business potential replaces the general intent weight in the finding's impact.
- **Format fit (I, 0–3):** whether your page is the kind of page that ranks (product, category, review, article, tool, …), from the stored top 10 of tracked keywords.
- **Rankability (D, 0–3):** one point each for difficulty within your limit, a weak result in the top 10 (a domain at or below your strength limit, or a forum thread) and an existing page-one ranking.
- **Verdict:** *Target*, *Consider* or *Reconsider*. Filter the list by verdict.

**Check competitor strength** on the business profile page rates the domains in your stored results pages in one DataForSEO request (the cost is shown first). Without it, rankability uses difficulty, forum results and your position.

### Zero-click risk

Each keyword finding shows a zero-click risk estimate: **high**, **medium** or **low**. It is higher when Google shows an AI Overview or an answer box, when the search asks for a definition or a quick fact, and when your click-through rate is far below what the position usually gets. It is lower when the search asks for comparisons, a purchase or a tool. A high risk lowers the confidence, not the estimate, and never hides the finding: you decide whether the clicks are worth it.

### Topics

Keyword findings name their **topic cluster**: keywords that share top results or subject words and that one page can usually target together. Question wording such as *how long does … last* or *types of* never links two different subjects.

Mark an opportunity **done** or **dismiss** it. If the underlying problem disappears, it moves to *resolved* by itself. **Analyze now** runs the analysis immediately. It is free, because it uses only data already on your server.

## Seeds and modifiers

*Keywords → Keyword research → Seeds and modifiers* builds a keyword list from short topics:

1. **Suggest seeds with AI** (needs the business profile and the AI assistant): the assistant proposes seed topics of one or two words and modifiers such as *best*, *how to*, *near me* or *calculator*. These are words to look up, not data. It is one model call, counted against the AI budget.
2. **Expand seeds** looks up the longer searches that contain each seed (up to 10 seeds, up to 100 searches each), with search volume, difficulty, intent and whether Google shows an AI Overview. Each seed is one DataForSEO request; the cost is shown.
3. Filter the result: **Contains one of your modifiers**, a single modifier, or **Tool searches only**. The Topic column groups searches one page can target.

Modifiers only filter the results; SEOcc never multiplies seeds and modifiers into paid queries.

## Relevance before and after paid research

The business profile also decides what is worth paying for:

- **Markets.** Under *Business profile → Markets you sell in*, list the countries and languages you sell in. A paid lookup in another market shows a notice and needs **Run anyway** ticked before anything is spent. With no markets set, nothing is checked.
- **Seeds that cannot fit are left out.** For *Expand seeds* and *Keyword ideas*, seeds with a term you exclude, and job or salary searches, are removed before the lookup is paid for. The message after queueing lists them with the reason. Tick **Run anyway** to include them.
- **Every result gets a verdict.** Keyword tables show **Relevant** (mentions something you offer), **Unsure** (names none of your offerings; wording alone cannot tell) or **Not relevant** (an excluded term or a job search), with the reason on hover. Not relevant keywords are hidden by default; the count below the table links to show them, and the **Relevance** filter switches between all keywords and only the hidden ones.
- **You decide.** Click *relevant?* or *not relevant?* next to a verdict to override it, or *reset* to go back to the rules. The override is the keyword's business-potential rating (not relevant = 0, relevant = 2), so opportunities use it too from the next analysis.

## Article ideas

*Research → Article ideas* suggests articles to write or update next, from the searches your competitors' articles rank for.

1. **Competitors.** SEOcc compares you with your tracked competitors, then with the sites it sees most often in your stored results pages (marked *found*). Big platforms such as Wikipedia, YouTube or Reddit are left out. At most 5 sites are used.
2. **Markets.** A lookup covers every market the project targets (a market is a country and language, such as *United States · English*). SEOcc takes them in this order:
   - the markets in the project's **business profile** (*Opportunities → Business profile*), at most 20;
   - without markets there, the markets of your **tracked keywords**, the market with the most keywords first;
   - without keywords, *United States · English*.

   The page says which of these was used, with a link to the business profile: add, remove or reorder markets there to change them. Markets that DataForSEO Labs has no competitor data for (such as *Germany · English*) are skipped and named on the page; they are never looked up or paid for.
3. **Find article ideas** buys up to 500 ranked keywords per competitor and market from DataForSEO. The cost grows with both: competitors × markets × the price of one lookup. With several markets the page shows that sum and the cost per market; tick the confirmation to pay. The run buys exactly the competitors and markets you confirmed: if they changed after the page was shown and the cost went up, the run is refused and you confirm the new cost. If the last lookup is under 30 days old, a second tick is needed: competitor rankings change slowly. The lookup runs in the background; ideas appear within a few minutes.
4. **Only articles count.** Competitor pages that look like blog posts, guides, how-tos or reviews are used, when they rank on page one or two (position 20 or better). Product, category and home pages are not. Searches under 10 a month, and searches your business profile or keyword ratings rule out, are skipped. Each search goes to the competitor article that ranks best for it, and one article makes one idea. Copies of one article in another language or country folder (/blog-… and /us/blog-…) count as one article, and articles that each rank in the top 10 for the other's main search are combined. Close variants that Google gives one shared search volume (*slicer vs paste*, *paste vs slicer plants*) are counted once.
5. **Per market.** Ideas are built for each market from that market's rankings, with your relevance rules applied to each. When the same search is an idea in several markets of the same language (*how to grow tomatoes* in the United States and Canada), it is listed once: its volume and traffic add the markets up, and a table on the idea shows the split per market (searches, clicks, difficulty and competitor articles). Difficulty and time to rank are those of its hardest market. The same words in another language stay a separate idea, and volumes of different languages are never added up.

Each idea says what to do:

- **New article:** none of your pages ranks within the top 30 for the topic.
- **Update your article:** one of your articles or guides ranks between 4 and 30. Improving it is usually faster. When only a shop page (a product or listing) ranks, the idea is a new article, which can link to that page.
- Topics where you already rank in the top 3 are left out.

Each idea also shows estimates, as ranges with how they were made:

- **Traffic:** clicks a month at positions 9 to 2, from the topic's search volume and your site's click-through by position.
- **Difficulty:** low, medium or hard, from keyword difficulty, the referring domains of the pages on page one and your own domain's links.
- **Backlinks to speed it up:** referring domains that would put the article in line with page one. Internal links and your domain carry part of it.
- **Time to rank:** a rough range of months by difficulty. It is an assumption until SEOcc has enough of your own ranking history.

With several markets, each idea names its market or markets, and a **Market** filter above the ideas shows one market at a time. With one market the page looks as before.

Open *Competitor articles and searches* to see the competitor pages, their positions and estimated traffic, the searches with volume and difficulty, and your page. **Hide** removes an idea; **Not relevant** also marks its main search as not relevant for future research. Ideas are rebuilt every day for free from the stored lookup, so they follow your rankings; hidden ideas stay hidden. **Rebuild ideas now** does the same right away, for free (up to 6 times an hour), for example after an update or a change to your business profile. Rebuilds use the stored rankings of every market of the last lookup and never buy anything; a market you add to the business profile is only looked up with the next paid lookup. The top 3 ideas also appear on the Opportunities page.

### Competitor outlines and briefs

**Read competitor outlines** on an idea reads its top 3 competitor articles, for free. It also reads your page when the idea is an update.

- SEOcc reads them like page comparisons do: HTTPS only, robots.txt respected. It keeps only their headings and word counts, never the text.
- The read runs in the background; refresh the page after a few minutes.
- An idea can be read once a week; a failed read can be repeated straight away.

The idea then shows its **subtopics**: headings that articles of at least two competitor sites share, most widely covered first. SEOcc reads one article per site first and uses only each article's own headings. Menus, footers, cookie and privacy notices are skipped, and so are headings a site repeats on all its articles. If only one site could be read, its headings are shown. For an update, each subtopic is marked ✓ when your page has it, or *missing on your page*. Questions the articles answer in their headings are listed too: those that name the idea's main search, or that two sites ask. *Competitor outlines* shows each article's headings, or why it couldn't be read.

**Create brief** opens a new content brief filled in from the idea:

- the target search and related searches;
- an outline with the main search as H1 and the subtopics as H2s;
- the questions to answer and, for an update, what is missing on your page;
- for an update, your page as the URL;
- evidence: the idea's market or markets, volume, estimates, the competitor articles and when their outlines were read.

Read the outlines first to get the subtopics into the brief. Review and edit everything before you save.

AI assistants can read the ideas, with their outlines and subtopics, using the `article_ideas` tool (*Keywords* permission).

### Did the prediction hold?

When an article from an idea is live, open the idea and choose **Mark as published**. Enter the article's address on your site and the date. A content brief whose target search is the idea's main search does the same once you save it as *Published* with its address.

**Published articles** at the top of *Article ideas* then compares the prediction with what happened, from your Search Console data, checked every morning:

- **Clicks/month now:** from the last four weeks, next to the predicted range.
- **Top 10 for the main search:** after how many months the main search first reached an average position of 10 or better (in a week with at least 10 impressions), or how long it has been so far.
- **Best position:** the best weekly position across the article's searches.

The prediction shown is the one made when you marked the article, even if the idea changes or disappears later (for example once you rank in the top 3).

Once **3 tracked articles** of the same kind (new or update) and difficulty reached the top 10, new *time to rank* estimates for that kind and difficulty use your site's own range instead of the assumption. The estimate's note then says so. **Stop tracking** removes an article from the list; the idea stays.

### Topic plans

**Plan a topic** on an article idea makes it the *pillar* of a topic plan, for free. Use it for an article that should cover a subject broadly, with supporting articles around it. Plans are listed under *Research → Topic plans*.

SEOcc proposes three kinds of members; tick the ones to keep and **Save plan**:

- **Supporting articles:** other article ideas on the pillar's subject, in a language of the pillar's markets. The subject is the pillar's rarest words. For "mold on pepper" it is *mold*, because *pepper* appears in most of your searches.
- **Searches to consider:** your Search Console queries on the subject that no idea covers. They start unticked; keep one to plan an article for it.
- **Your pages:** pages that already get impressions on the subject. They should link to the pillar.

The **link map** is built in the background:

- links between the pillar and each kept article (with their main searches as anchor text);
- links from your kept pages to the pillar;
- places on your crawled pages that already mention a planned article's search, with the paragraph and the words to link. This needs a finished site audit. Add those links once the article is published. **Rebuild link map** refreshes it after a new audit.

**Check backlinks** buys the backlinks of the pillar's top 2 competitor pages from DataForSEO (about $0.05; tick the confirmation). The plan shows their referring domains, backlinks and page rank, and about how many referring domains would put your pillar level with the strongest one. A second check within 30 days needs another tick.

**Create brief** works for the pillar and every supporting article. A brief made from a planned idea lists the plan's links under *Internal links to add*. AI assistants can read plans with the `topic_plans` tool (*Keywords* permission).

## Topics and page owners

*Keywords → Topics & owners* lists the topics the opportunity analysis found: searches from Search Console, tracked keywords and research that one page can target together. Searches your business profile rules out (excluded terms, job searches, keywords marked not relevant) are left out, and a topic is named after its top remaining search. By default the list shows topics with at least one search that names what you offer, or that your site already gets traffic or rankings for, or that you gave an owner. The others are counted in a note; choose **Show all topics** to see them. A tracked keyword is always a topic, even alone, and searches whose results pages show the same three or more sites in the top 10 are grouped together. Topics are saved after every analysis, so run **Analyze now** if the page is empty.

- **Owner.** The page that gets most of the topic's clicks in Search Console (or impressions, when there are under 10 clicks) owns it. Pages of one listing (`?page=2`, `/page/3/`) count as one page. Under 5 clicks and 50 impressions in total there is too little data, so no owner is named; the leading page is still listed. Without Search Console data, the page your rank checks find most often. **Contested** means a second page is close (at least 20 % and at least 60 % of the leader's share): decide which one should own the topic. **Unowned** means no page shows up yet; a new or improved page could take it.
- **Set the owner yourself** with *Page that should own this topic*. Your choice stays when the analysis runs again; SEOcc still tells you if Search Console sends the traffic elsewhere. *Use Search Console again* removes your choice.
- **Overlap.** Under each topic, searches that more than one of your pages appears for are labelled from 8 weeks of data:
  - *Switching pages*: the leading page changed at least twice. Google cannot decide; make one page clearly the best answer and link to it from the other.
  - *Split*: one page leads, but another takes a real share. Check whether they answer different questions before merging or redirecting.
  - *Two listings*: the same page leads and the other appears next to it on page one. Usually good.
  - *Brand search*: your name with the home page among the results. Normal.

## Why they outrank you

Choose **Why they outrank you** next to a topic in *Topics & owners* to find out what kind of page Google ranks for it, how the competing pages of that kind differ from yours, and what to change.

- **Cost.** When SEOcc stored the results page for the topic's main search in the last 14 days (from rank checks or opportunity research), the analysis is free. Otherwise it needs one DataForSEO results-page lookup; the page shows the estimated cost and you confirm it before anything is spent. Without DataForSEO and without a recent stored page, the analysis cannot run and the page says why.
- **Reading the pages.** The analysis runs in the background. Your server reads up to five competing pages and your own page (the topic owner, or your ranking URL) directly, over HTTPS only, and respects each site's robots.txt. Pages that block it, need a login or show a bot challenge are listed as *blocked* and left out; forums, videos and marketplaces count towards the format but are never read. Only page structure is stored (title, headings, word count, schema types, page elements, dates), never the competitors' text.
- **What Google wants.** Every result on the page is classified (article, product, category, tool, forum, video and so on) from its schema and page elements, or from its address when it was not read, with a confidence. The format is *dominant* when one type takes at least 60 % of the weighted results, *mixed* when two types each take at least 25 %, and *fragmented* otherwise.
- **Main bottleneck.** One of *technical* (your page could not be read), *format* (Google prefers another page type), *content gaps* (same-type competitors cover subtopics you do not), *freshness* (they were updated recently, your page was not) or *unclear*.
- **Actions.** Up to seven concrete changes, each with the competing pages it was seen on and an effort: create a page of the right type, pair your page with one of the other type, fix the technical problem, add or expand sections, add schema or media, refresh the page, or improve the title. When the format differs, SEOcc never tells you to rewrite your page into another type; it suggests a second page and linking the two.
- **Opportunities.** The actions of each topic's latest analysis (up to 30 days old) become opportunities at the next analysis, with the evidence and an estimated gain, so they are ranked and tracked with your other findings.

- **AI explanation.** With the AI assistant set up (*Integrations → AI assistant*), the analysis also asks your AI model once to explain the findings: a short verdict, a page plan (which page should target which searches), specific instructions and a suggested outline for each action, and things to avoid. The model only explains what the rules found; anything that names an unknown address or would turn a page into another type is dropped. The cost is shown before you analyze and comes from the AI budget. Without the assistant you get the same findings without the written explanation.
- **Internal links.** From your latest complete site audit, SEOcc recommends up to five links that make the topic's pages work together: supporting guides to the main page and back, the category page to the product, and strong related pages that do not link yet. Each comes with two or three anchors from the target's real Search Console searches and where to place it. Links only point to the page that owns the topic (or its main shop page); when no page owns the topic yet, the section says so and recommends none. Pages with very few internal links, and pages that compete for the same searches (merge or split them instead of linking them), are flagged. Without a site audit, the section says so. Each target page becomes one internal-links opportunity.
- **Client report.** **Client report (PDF)** downloads the analysis as a PDF with the report branding set under *Reports*, ready to send to a client.

Run **Analyze again** after you change the page. Only one analysis per topic runs at a time, and a finished analysis is reused for 14 days unless you choose to analyze again.

### Did the change work?

When you mark an opportunity done, SEOcc records the clicks of the 28 days before and measures again after 28 and 56 days: **Opportunities → Predicted vs observed**. Each row also says whether the work was really done:

- **Verified: page changed**: page monitoring saw the page change within 14 days of completion. The page is the one set on the team task, otherwise the finding's page. Watch the page beforehand (see [Page monitoring](25-page-monitoring.md)) to get this automatically.
- **Confirmed** or **Not done**: an editor chose **Confirm done** or **Not done** (on the day-28 row; it applies to both checkpoints). Results marked not done no longer count when SEOcc adjusts its estimates.
- **Not verified**: neither of the above.

**Overlaps** lists other changes in the same window: change notes for the whole site or the same page, other completed opportunities for the same search or page, and later changes detected on the page. The result may then not come from this change alone. Once a type has five verified or confirmed results without overlaps, SEOcc adjusts its estimates from those alone. Measured results remain correlation, not proof.

## Team work from opportunities

Choose Manage task on a finding to assign work, set a deadline and keep notes. The separate Team tasks view filters assignments and progress without replacing SEO finding statuses. Link writing briefs and recorded changes, then review their impact. See [SEO team tasks](24-seo-team-tasks.md).

08.title: 8. AI access (MCP)
08.text:
# 8. AI access (MCP)

AI assistants such as Claude can read your SEO data through the **Model Context Protocol (MCP)**. You can then ask questions like "Which pages lost clicks this month?" or "Where is seedhouse.com ahead of us?".

Access is **read-only** unless you allow changes: you can let an assistant add change notes, update team tasks, write content briefs, set opportunity status and start or stop page watches. It can never delete anything or start paid lookups.

## Create a token

1. Go to **Integrations → AI access → New token**. Owners and admins can do this.
2. Enter a name, for example "Claude Desktop".
3. Choose the **data** it may read, including **Pages** for URL-level insights. Existing tokens need a new explicit grant for `pages:read`.
4. Optionally tick the **changes** it may make. Nothing is ticked by default.
5. Choose **all projects** or only some.
6. Choose an **expiry** (30, 90 or 365 days, or never).

The token (`scc_…`) is shown **once**. Copy it into your AI client right away. You can revoke tokens at any time on the same page.

## Connect your AI client

- **Server URL:** `https://seo.example.com/mcp`
- **Authentication:** header `Authorization: Bearer scc_…`
- **Transport:** Streamable HTTP

**Claude Code** (terminal):

```
claude mcp add --transport http seo-control-center https://seo.example.com/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer scc_YOUR_TOKEN"
```

Other MCP clients: add a remote (HTTP) MCP server with the URL and header above.

## Connect ChatGPT

ChatGPT connects with a sign-in instead of a token. You need a paid ChatGPT plan (Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise or Edu).

1. In ChatGPT, open **Settings → Apps & Connectors → Advanced settings** and turn on **Developer mode**.
2. Click **Create** (or *Add custom connector*). Enter a name such as "SEO Control Center" and the **server URL** shown under *Integrations → AI access*, for example `https://seo.example.com/mcp`, and choose **OAuth** as the authentication.
3. ChatGPT opens a sign-in page of SEO Control Center. Sign in if needed, choose the **workspace** and the **data** ChatGPT may read, and click **Allow**.

ChatGPT then appears in the token list as "ChatGPT (sign-in)". To disconnect, revoke that token. Only owners and admins can connect apps. Claude.ai custom connectors work the same way.

## What the assistant can use

The assistant can read the public guide through `guide_list`, `guide_search` and `guide_read`. These explain how SEOcc features work without exposing internal developer documents. Ask it to consult the guide when you need setup or workflow instructions.

It can also read a scoped project overview, stored GA4 landing-page outcomes and daily coverage, project alerts and report schedule/section status. Workspace spending totals require administrator permissions. Saved audits, backlinks, AI visibility, local branches, annotations, change impact, content briefs, indexing and team tasks remain available through their dedicated tools. Recipient addresses, credentials and private configuration are excluded.

For useful answers, specify the project, dates and page or keyword. Large lists return limited pages or clearly labelled samples; the assistant should inspect coverage and fetch another page only when needed. Google/Bing search dates can cover up to 486 days; GA4 ranges up to 365 days. Missing imports and incomplete or thresholded analytics must not be treated as zero.
